blockers.summary: libnss-db has been removed from Debian and from the Tenacious development release. The fix therefore cannot land in the development series first, as SRU policy requires. The open Tenacious MR is moot, and the SRU team would need to explicitly accept an Ubuntu-only SRU for a package that no longer exists in the devel release.

The patch is an Ubuntu-only delta. Upstream is abandoned, Debian has not merged it, and glibc showed no interest. The risk of stale DB data after external updates (the close/reopen behaviour was possibly there for CVE-2014-8121-style reasons) is only asserted, not tested.

The test plan is vague. Step 7 gives no concrete strace or ltrace command, no expected open/close counts, and no before/after comparison. It also has no check for behaviour when the DB file is updated while a process is running. The steps (for example 'make' in /var/lib/misc and the typos) may not be reproducible as written.

The Stonking version string may need to be ubuntu0.1 rather than ubuntu1 if the fix will not reach the devel release before it ships. The debdiffs were superseded by MRs, and it is unclear whether versions, changelog entries, and maintainer fields were corrected there.

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is set, and the fix depends on OVN support for it, so the SRU may not resolve the problem for default deployments. The reporter's OVN version (23.03) predates the OVN 24.09 fix mentioned for the related E/W bug (LP #2085099), so the SRU should state the required OVN version and configuration.

The upstream fix regressed (LP #2105383: redirect-type calculation wrongly included the gateway port). The stable backports combine both commits, so the SRU must include the follow-up revert, and the Ubuntu package must not take only the first commit. The backports also needed unit and functional test conflict changes, so testing should be confirmed.

blockers.summary: The SRU reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced or understood from the boot side, so it is unclear whether the patch is correct. The test plan only shows reproducing the bug and says the entry will not appear after the fix. It has no explicit verification steps for the fixed package, and nothing checks that other filesystems, such as NTFS or a dual-boot install, are still detected.

comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
